name: Peripheral Neuropathy Associated with Monoclonal Gammopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for MGUS-Associated Peripheral Neuropathy

criteria.description: Presence of a monoclonal gammopathy confirmed by serum or urine protein electrophoresis and immunofixation
Clinical evidence of peripheral neuropathy characterized by distal symmetric sensory or sensorimotor deficits
Electrodiagnostic studies confirming peripheral nerve involvement consistent with demyelinating or axonal neuropathy
Exclusion of alternative causes of neuropathy such as diabetes, vitamin deficiencies, or other systemic diseases
Nerve biopsy showing demyelination, axonal loss, or deposition of monoclonal protein (optional supportive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of monoclonal gammopathy plus clinical and electrophysiological evidence of peripheral neuropathy with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including hematology and neurology consultation.

searchTerms: loss of feeling in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Monoclonal protein presence in serum or urine
searchTerms: abnormal protein in blood or urine

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes

occasional.symptomName: Neuropathic pain with burning or shooting quality
searchTerms: tingling burning pain in arms or legs
nerve problems in head or face
mild problems with balance and coordination
impaired coordination due to sensory loss
hands and feet sensitive to cold
cold intolerance in fingers and toes

occasional.symptomName: Mild skin changes such as dryness or trophic changes
searchTerms: mild dry or thin skin changes

rare.symptomName: Severe autonomic neuropathy with gastrointestinal dysmotility
searchTerms: severe nerve dysfunction with digestive issues
nerve symptoms from blood vessel inflammation
nerve and organ damage from abnormal protein

laboratory: Serum and urine protein electrophoresis with immunofixation showing monoclonal protein
Elevated serum free light chains ratio
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: Nerve ultrasound may show nerve enlargement
MRI may show nerve root or plexus hypertrophy in some cases
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; monoclonal gammopathy is a clonal plasma cell disorder
other: Nerve conduction studies demonstrating demyelinating or axonal neuropathy
Nerve biopsy showing demyelination, axonal loss, or monoclonal protein deposits

distinguishingFeatures: Symmetric distal sensory loss without monoclonal protein
May or may not have monoclonal gammopathy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
Signs of systemic amyloidosis (e.g., nephrotic syndrome, cardiomyopathy)
Severe autonomic dysfunction causing syncope or gastrointestinal dysmotility
references: Dispenzieri A, Kyle RA. Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance and Related Disorders. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2005.
Rajkumar SV. Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance. N Engl J Med. 2005.
Dalakas MC. Peripheral neuropathy associated with monoclonal gammopathies. Nat Rev Neurol. 2015.
